OMAR: Welcome to My Clinic. I'm Dr. Omar, a family physician at J2. Today you'll meet who we are, and the HR rules you'll actually use. NOOR: And I'm Noor, a senior nurse at J1. Nothing here is a memory test. We'll show you where to find things.

Why we exist

Purpose — helping people live longer, healthier, happier lives

Mission — the world's most customer-centric healthcare company

Goal — outstanding patient experience + excellent clinical outcomes

OMAR: Our purpose is simple to say and hard to do: we help people live longer, healthier, happier lives, including people who are well today. Our mission is to be the world's most customer-centric healthcare company. In practice, every role asks one question: did this help the patient? Our goal follows from that: outstanding patient experience, alongside excellent clinical outcomes. Honestly, my first week here, I felt there was too much to take in. You don't need to remember everything today — just where to find it.

One million riyals

If you had one million Saudi riyals, where would you spend it?

Whatever you chose says something you care about. At My Clinic, we start from what people care about — including yours.

OMAR: Before we start: if you had one million Saudi riyals, where would you spend it? There's no right answer. Pick whatever is closest.

Our four values

Values are behaviours. Open each one and look for something you already do.

Unites diverse

Creating a culture of accountability

Own our decisions and actions · Make things happen · Demonstrate high professional standards · Hold yourself and each other accountable

Set new standards

Go above and beyond · Make new possibilities happen · Challenge the status quo · Become industry shapers · Deliver outstanding results

Putting empathy first

Act with empathy · Everyone matters · Love our customers · Deliver with quality

OMAR: Every clinic has values on a wall. Ours only matter if you can see them in what people do. Collaborative: we act together, treat everyone with respect, and stay transparent. Responsible: own your decisions, make things happen, and hold each other to the same standard. Ambitious: go above and beyond, and challenge the status quo when it stops serving patients. Caring: act with empathy, because everyone matters. As you go on, think which of these you already do without being asked.

Which pillar?

My Care follow-up calls that build patient loyalty support which pillar?

Care. My Care follow-up calls are named in the Care pillar under “build loyalty through My Care”. Loyalty is a service and relationship outcome, not an access outcome.

Closer covers access: physical, community and home health care, digital services, and the call centre and telemedicine. A phone call is access; a follow-up call that builds loyalty is Care.

Culture is mission, values and servant leadership. It shapes how we behave, not this service.

Cost is about cost to serve: revenue cycle, efficiency and overhead. Loyalty work sits on the service side.

Our code of ethics

Respect — uphold the rights, privacy and dignity of patients, families and colleagues.

Integrity — transparent practice; disclose any potential conflict of interest.

Accountability — a culture that encourages reporting safety concerns and adherence to policy.

Innovation & collaboration — support research and community engagement to improve quality and outcomes.

Ethical dilemma? Incident report within 24 hours + ethics team. Pending B14 / D8.

OMAR: Four values sit under everything. Respect — the rights, privacy and dignity of patients, families and colleagues. Integrity — be transparent, and disclose any conflict of interest. Accountability — a culture where people report safety concerns instead of staying quiet. Innovation and collaboration — research and community work that improves outcomes. And the rule you'll use: faced with an ethical dilemma, complete an incident report within twenty-four hours and bring in the ethics team. You're never expected to work it out alone.

A supplier you know

Noor · Safety liaison

Three moments, three decisions. Nobody is watching.

Score: 0

You're on a panel evaluating three suppliers for a clinic fit-out. One bidder is your cousin's company. The evaluation starts in an hour.

  • Even a fair score looks compromised. Integrity means disclosing a potential conflict of interest before the work starts, in procurement as much as in recruitment.

  • Right. You disclose the potential conflict and remove yourself from the decision. Nobody has to guess afterwards, including you.

  • Leaving is better than scoring, but silence doesn't help: the panel still doesn't know why, and the conflict stays undocumented. Declare it, then step back.

A colleague from another department asks you to “help” a patient skip the queue, and offers you a gift.

  • Right. Fair access is part of Respect — every patient in that queue is waiting for the same reason. A gift makes it a transaction.

  • Returning the gift afterwards doesn't undo it. Someone else waited longer because of a favour, and the gift makes it a transaction.

  • Quiet or not, that patient is still moving ahead of people who waited. Decline, and say why.

A week later you're not sure whether something you saw counts as an ethical issue. Nobody else has raised it.

  • Waiting is the common mistake. The policy doesn't ask you to be certain; it asks you to act on the dilemma you have.

  • Right. Consult colleagues for anything beyond your expertise, and complete an incident report within twenty-four hours so the ethics team can guide you. That's Accountability working.

  • A quiet word is a start, but it leaves no record and no route to advice. Report it within twenty-four hours and bring the ethics team in.

NOOR: Three moments now, and nobody is watching. First: you're on a panel evaluating suppliers for a clinic fit-out, and one bidder is your cousin's company. The evaluation starts in an hour. What do you do?

She said no

A patient refuses a blood test after the doctor has explained the risks. What is the right response?

Right. Refusal of treatment is a patient right once the risks are understood. Your job is to check understanding, document the refusal, and inform the doctor.

Bringing in a manager to talk her round turns a right into pressure. She can refuse once she understands the risks.

Proceeding against a competent patient's refusal is not consent. Stop and escalate to the doctor instead.

A family member cannot replace her consent. Only she can decide, once she understands the risks.

Leave at a glance

Nine types. Open the one you need — the full tables are in the Quick Reference.

Annual

After probation, with your line manager's approval. Carry over up to 5 days; use them by end of March (consulting-room physicians: end of June). Pending B9.

Sick

Tell your line manager. Valid medical report required. First 30 days full pay; days 31–90 pending B1; days 91–120 unpaid.

Work injury

Covers work hours and commuting. Report to your line manager and HR the same day or the next day.

Maternity

12 weeks. You may start up to 4 weeks before the expected delivery date.

Exam

Paid, for academic exams only. Actual exam days only. Documents at least 2 weeks in advance. IELTS, TOEFL and similar are not eligible.

Scientific

Paid days per profession each year, for academic exams. Needs the MD's pre-approval. Cannot be carried over. Pending B10.

Hajj

Muslim employees with two full years of service. 10–15 days including Eid. Hajj permit copy required. Pending B11.

Compassionate

Marriage 5 days · paternity 3 · immediate relative 5 · sibling 3 · death of a husband pending B2.

Official holidays

Eid al-Fitr 4 days · Eid al-Adha 4 days · Founding Day 22 February · National Day 23 September.

OMAR: Nine types. Open the ones you need. Annual: after probation, five days carried over, used by end of March. Sick: valid report needed. First thirty days paid in full. Work injury covers commuting, and has a same-day or next-day deadline. Maternity: twelve weeks, starting up to four weeks early. Exam leave: academic exams only, documents two weeks ahead. Scientific: by profession, and can't be carried over. Hajj: two years' service and a permit. Compassionate: marriage, paternity, bereavement. Then Eid, Founding Day, National Day. We'll practise the four people ask about most.

Forty days of sick leave

A colleague is off sick for 40 days in one year, with valid medical reports from My Clinic. How is the pay worked out?

  1. 1Step 1

    Days 1–30 — tell your line manager you are unwell.

    Notification is the first requirement. Sick leave is accepted only with a valid medical report, and your manager needs to know today, not at the end of it.

  2. 2Step 2

    Days 1–30 — full salary.

    The first thirty days of valid sick leave in a year are paid in full.

  3. 3Step 3

    Days 31–40 — reduced pay. Per the slide as written: 25% deducted, so 75% of salary. Pending B1.

    The second band cuts pay by a quarter. Continuous and separated periods count the same way, so the band follows the total days in the year, not one absence.

  4. 4Step 4

    Days 91–120 — unpaid.

    The bands run 1–30, 31–90 and 91–120. Forty days never reaches this band, but it's the ceiling you should know.

  5. 5Step 5

    Check the report: from outside My Clinic, it needs Staff Health Clinic approval.

    Reports from My Clinic are accepted as they are. Anything from another provider has to be approved, or the leave isn't valid.

What changes if the medical report comes from another hospital?

Not graded
OMAR: One example, properly. A colleague is off sick forty days in a year, with valid reports. First, she tells her line manager — that's first, not last. The first thirty days are paid in full. Ten days fall into the next band, and that's where pay drops. Note the detail people miss: it's the total in the year that sets the band, not one spell. Beyond ninety days it's unpaid. And if the report is from outside My Clinic, the Staff Health Clinic must approve it. Now: what changes if her report comes from another hospital?

The leave desk

Noor · Safety liaison

Four colleagues, four questions. You're the one they've asked.

Score: 0

Yousuf is a lab technician. He asks for two days of scientific leave, and he already has the MD's pre-approval for his documents. How many days can he take this year?

  • Right. Scientific leave is 2 days a year for lab and radiology technicians, 3 for nurses, 4 for pharmacists, 5 for other physicians and dentists, and 7 for consultants. It also can't be carried over.

  • Seven days is the consultants' allowance. Technicians get two. The allowance follows the profession, not the request.

  • Not so. Every profession in the table has an allowance; technicians have the smallest, at two days a year.

  • The days are right, the carry-over isn't. Scientific leave cannot be carried over — unused days are lost.

Amal is a nurse. She asks for exam leave to sit IELTS next month, and she has her documents ready.

  • Right. Exam leave is paid leave for academic examinations only, and IELTS, TOEFL and Microsoft certifications are named as not eligible. Having the documents ready doesn't change eligibility.

  • Documents matter, but eligibility comes first. IELTS is not an academic examination and is named as not eligible.

  • Well meant, but the rule is about the type of exam, not the number of days. IELTS is not eligible, so there are no days to approve.

Reem is a pharmacist with one full year of service. She asks for Hajj leave and has her Hajj permit ready.

  • Right. Two full years of continuous service is the eligibility rule, and one year doesn't meet it. The permit is needed, but it doesn't shorten the service requirement.

  • It isn't. Hajj leave is for Muslim employees with two full years of continuous service.

  • The permit is a requirement, not a substitute. Without two full years of service she isn't eligible, permit or not.

Sara is a receptionist. She slipped on the way into work this morning and her ankle is painful. What does she need to do?

  • Right. Work injury covers commuting as well as work hours, and the deadline is the same day or the following day. HR then reports the case to GOSI.

  • Waiting is the mistake this rule exists to prevent. The report has to go to her line manager and HR the same day or the next day, whether or not she ends up taking time off.

  • They are. Work injury applies during work hours and while commuting to and from work, for Saudi and expatriate employees alike.

Leave rules: quick practice

Answer until the practice says you're ready. It stops early if you've got it.

0 / 6

How many unused annual leave days can you carry over?

Carry-over is capped at 5 days. Anything above that is lost at the end of the carry-over window.

The cap is a small number — single digits.

Carried-over annual leave must be used by when?

Carried-over leave has to be used by the end of March of the following year.

It's the end of a spring month.

A consulting-room physician carries over leave. By when must it be used?

Consulting-room physicians have a later deadline: the end of June.

This group gets three months more than everyone else.

How long is maternity leave?

Maternity leave is 12 weeks.

It's measured in weeks, not months — and it's the longest of the three options.

How early can maternity leave start?

You may start up to 4 weeks before the expected delivery date.

The allowance is measured in weeks before the due date.

Exam leave documents must be submitted how far in advance?

Documents — the exam schedule and course schedule, plus a result transcript afterwards — must go in at least two weeks in advance.

Think in weeks, and it's more than one.

How many days of leave for your own marriage?

Marriage leave is 5 calendar days.

Marriage attracts the same number of days as bereavement of an immediate relative.

How many days of paternity leave?

Paternity leave is 3 days.

It's the same number as bereavement of a sibling.

Bereavement leave for the death of a sibling?

Death of a sibling is 3 calendar days. Death of an immediate relative — spouse, parent or child — is 5.

Immediate relatives attract more days than siblings.

How many days is each Eid holiday?

Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha are each 4 days.

Both Eids are the same length.

When is Founding Day?

Founding Day is 22 February. National Day is 23 September — the two are easy to swap.

It's a February date, and the other national holiday falls in September.

Can unused scientific leave be carried over?

Scientific leave cannot be carried over. It also needs the MD's pre-approval, but approval doesn't create a carry-over.

Approval and carry-over are two different rules; only one of them is mentioned in the source.

OMAR: A short practice set now. It adapts: if you're getting these, it will finish early. If you're not, it'll keep going for a few more.

What GOSI is

GOSI — General Organization for Social Insurance.

Saudi employees only, until retirement at 60.

9.75% you + 11.75% My Clinic = 21.5% of basic + housing. Rates pending B12.

OMAR: GOSI is the General Organization for Social Insurance — the government body for social protection in Saudi Arabia. It applies to Saudi employees, until retirement at sixty. The split matters: you pay nine point seven five per cent of basic plus housing. My Clinic pays eleven point seven five. So the real contribution is twenty-one point five, and most of it isn't yours.

Working out 585 riyals

Basic 4,800 + housing 1,200. What is the monthly GOSI deduction from your salary? Rates pending B12.

  1. 1Step 1

    Add basic and housing: 4,800 + 1,200 = 6,000.

    GOSI is charged on basic salary plus housing allowance, not on basic alone and not on total pay with allowances and bonuses.

  2. 2Step 2

    Apply the employee rate: 6,000 × 9.75%.

    Only your share is deducted from your salary. The company's 11.75% is paid on top and never appears as a deduction on your payslip.

  3. 3Step 3

    Result: 585 SAR deducted each month.

    6,000 × 0.0975 = 585. This is the line you'll see on your payslip.

Which part of the salary is the percentage applied to?

Not graded
OMAR: Let's do one together. Basic four thousand eight hundred, housing one thousand two hundred. Add them — GOSI is charged on basic plus housing, so six thousand. Apply your rate, nine point seven five per cent. The company's rate never touches your payslip. Six thousand times nought point nought nine seven five is five hundred and eighty-five riyals a month. That's the line to look for.

Your turn

Basic 6,000 + housing 1,500. Your monthly GOSI deduction = ___ SAR. Rates pending B12.

OMAR: Your turn. Basic six thousand, housing one thousand five hundred. What's your monthly GOSI deduction?

Working out overtime

Basic 6,000. What is your overtime rate on a normal working day, and on a public holiday? Eligibility by grade pending B3.

  1. 1Step 1

    Hourly rate: 6,000 ÷ (30 × 8) = 6,000 ÷ 240 = 25 SAR/hour.

    The formula uses a 30-day month at 8 hours a day, so 240 hours. Everything else in the calculation hangs off this one number.

  2. 2Step 2

    Normal working day: 25 × 1.5 = 37.50 SAR/hour.

    Overtime on a normal working day is paid at time and a half.

  3. 3Step 3

    Public holiday: 25 × 2 = 50 SAR/hour.

    Overtime on a public holiday is paid at double time. Note it's the same hourly rate — only the multiplier changes.

Why is the hourly rate worked out from 240 hours, not 208?

Not graded
OMAR: One caveat before the numbers: whether you're eligible for overtime at all depends on your grade. Check that first. Now the arithmetic. Basic six thousand. Divide by thirty days times eight hours — two hundred and forty hours — and you get twenty-five riyals an hour. On a normal working day, multiply by one and a half. That's thirty-seven riyals fifty. On a public holiday, multiply by two. Fifty riyals an hour. Same hourly rate both times. Only the multiplier moves.

Four hours on Tuesday

Basic 6,000. You work 4 overtime hours on a normal working day. What is the overtime pay?

Right. Hourly rate is 6,000 ÷ 240 = 25, then 25 × 1.5 × 4 hours = 150 SAR.

That's 25 × 4. You've worked out the plain hourly pay and left out the time-and-a-half multiplier.

That's 25 × 2 × 4. Double time is for a public holiday, not a normal working day.

That doesn't come from the formula. Go back to the hourly rate first: 6,000 ÷ 240.

OMAR: One for you. Basic six thousand. You work four overtime hours on a normal working day. What's the overtime pay?

How you did

One row per objective. Anything below 70% comes with a suggestion.

Values & strategy—

Revisit the four values and the 7C pillars. The one to remember: Care is where My Care and patient loyalty sit.

Ethics & patients' rights—

Disclose conflicts early, never trade access to care, and when you're unsure, report within 24 hours. A right is what the patient can expect; a responsibility is what we ask of them.

Leave—

Check three things on every request: the type of leave, the eligibility rule, and the document. The tables are in the HR Quick Reference.

Pay & social insurance—

GOSI is basic plus housing × 9.75%. Overtime is basic ÷ 240, then × 1.5, or × 2 on a public holiday.

Systems & licences—

Requests go through Oracle. Contracts on Qiwa, licences on Mumaris, guides on the intranet. Renew your licence well before it expires.

ID, dress code & contracts—

Front office wears the uniform, the medical team wears scrubs and a coat, back office is business attire. Notice is two months both ways.
